title: Multiple Superconducting Phases under Pressure for Different Field Directions in UTe2
authors: Dai Aoki, Atsushi Miyake, Ai Nakamura, Yoshiya Homma, Dexin Li, Shota Mizuno, Georg Knebel, Daniel Braithwaite, Jean-Pascal Brison, Jacques Flouquet
abstract: The existence of multiple superconducting phases is a striking feature of UTe2, arising from the spin and orbital degrees of freedom and supporting a spin-triplet superconducting state. We present field-temperature phase diagrams under pressure for fields applied along the three principal crystallographic axes, as determined by AC calorimetry measurements. The pressure evolution of the multiple superconducting phases is highly anisotropic with respect to magnetic field direction, revealing rich superconducting phenomena arising from complex fluctuations.
summary: This work maps out the complex, anisotropic superconducting phase diagrams of UTe2 under applied pressure and magnetic fields. By measuring transitions along the three crystallographic axes, the authors reveal multiple superconducting phases and field-reentrant behavior. This highlights the intricate interplay between crystal structure, magnetism, and unconventional superconductivity in this material.
main_problem: The study investigates the existence and pressure/field dependence of multiple superconducting phases in UTe2, focusing on the anisotropy of these superconducting states.
main_result: UTe2 exhibits highly anisotropic superconducting behavior, showing field-reentrant superconductivity favored along the hard-magnetization axes, which is linked to complex fluctuations.
method: The research primarily uses AC calorimetry measurements to map out field-temperature (H-T) phase diagrams under varying applied pressures.
model_or_system: The physical system is UTe2, a material known for its spin-triplet superconducting state, whose properties are modulated by external pressure and magnetic fields.
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperatures (Tc), phase boundaries (SC1, SC2), upper critical fields (Hc2), and the anisotropy of these features with respect to crystallographic axes (a, b, c).
important_parameters: Applied pressure (P), magnetic field strength (H), and the direction of the applied field relative to the crystal axes.
main_assumptions: The mechanism for superconductivity is noted to be more complex than in simple ferromagnetic superconductors like URhGe.
figures_summary: The figures present H-T phase diagrams for fields applied along the a, b, and c axes at various pressures, illustrating the reentrant and anisotropic superconducting regimes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents the H-T phase diagrams for the three principal field directions (a, b, c) under pressure, comparing the observed superconducting evolution to known ferromagnetic superconductors.
why_interesting: The strong coupling between magnetic anisotropy, pressure, and unconventional superconductivity in UTe2 provides a rich platform for studying emergent quantum phases in strongly correlated electron systems.

Fig. 3. H–T phase diagrams for H ∥b-axis at different pressures in UTe2. The dotted lines indicate the metamagnetic transition field Hm, estimated from Refs. 16–18. The lines are guides to the eye.

Figure 4 shows the H–T phase diagrams at different pressures for H ∥c-axis. After Tc splits, the low-temperature transition lines associated with SC1 progressively contract with increasing pressure, as do those for H ∥b-axis. The Hc2 curves for the SC2 phase display a larger magnitude of the initial slope with increasing pressure, as also observed for H ∥b-axis. Unlike the case for H ∥b-axis, no metamagnetic transition is observed for H ∥c-axis. The SC2 phase appears to extend beyond 15 T.

Fig. 5. Angular dependence of the superconducting critical fields in (a) URhGe and (b) UTe2. SC, HR and Hm denote superconductivity, the spin-reorientation field and the metamagnetic transition field, respectively. In URhGe, the easy-magnetization axis is the c-axis, and the hard axes correspond to the b and a-axes. In UTe2, the magnetization easy axis is the a-axis, and the hard axes correspond to the b and c axes. The high-field data in URhGe are taken from Ref. 21. The data of UTe2 are taken from Refs. 19,22,23.
